newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Turkish leader starts visit to Kazakhstan.
newsitem.headline: Turkish leader starts visit to Kazakhstan.

text.p: Turkish President Suleyman Demirel began a two-day visit to Kazakhstan on Monday by describing relations with the Turkic-speaking central Asian country as eternal.
Demirel's visit coincided with celebrations marking the former Soviet republic's fifth anniversary of independence from Moscow.
"Kazakh-Turkish relations are eternal," Demirel told reporters shortly before meeting Kazakh President Nursultan Nazarbayev in the capital Almaty.
Turkey is active in the central Asian republics but five years after the collapse of the Soviet Union dreams of pan-Turkic ties have largely faded.
Turkey lacks the cash to extend its influence in the region. Oil pipelines and transport links are still largely routed through Russia, which means Moscow remains dominant in central Asia.
Demirel returns to Ankara on Tuesday.
